function.name: rag_search_tool
function.description:
Performs RAG search in text files and returns llm answer based on the search.
Supports the following attachment types:
- .pdf - application/pdf
- .txt - text/plain
- .doc - application/msword
- .docx - application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document
- .odt - application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text
- .ppt - application/vnd.ms-powerpoint
- .pptx - application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation
- .odp - application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation
- .png - image/png
- .jpg/jpeg - image/jpeg
- .bmp - image/bmp
- .tiff/tif - image/tiff
Should be used when user asks to search for information in files or to answer questions based on file content.
The tool does not see the conversation history and does not remember previous calls: every call is independent. Write the query as a complete, self-contained question and attach every file needed to answer it, including files from earlier messages.

query.description: A complete, self-contained question for the RAG search. The tool cannot see the conversation, so never use pronouns or references that depend on earlier messages ("it", "this country", "the previous document", "the first file"). Name the subject explicitly (names, titles, topics) and include all the context needed to understand the question.

attachment_urls.description: A list of full URLs for each attachment related to the tool call. Each item is a reference, never inline content: a DIAL file path (files/bucket/foo.pdf) or an external `https://` URL. Inline forms (`file:data::`, `file:base64::`, `file:text::`, a literal `data:` URI) are not accepted and will be rejected. *Always provide a list*, even if there is only one attachment. Do not provide a single string; use a list with one element instead. If there are no attachments, provide an empty list. Include every file the answer depends on, also those attached in earlier messages of the conversation: the tool searches only the files passed in this call and knows nothing about files from previous calls.
